timeline.tweet: Depression is a beast. Sending you 💖

I've been practicing this since high school. I'm constantly preparing for the worst, so it makes it hard to feel appreciative of the good things happen in the present. In essence, I've traded the joys of my present for pessimism about the future.
This, please. Don't underestimate depression. It makes your whole head an unsafe place for you to be. Get help. The National Suicide Prevention Line is always there: 1-800-273-8255

Setbacks: I'm only going to unique setbacks because the old ones (unemployment, poorness) are still there. Until they move to the success column, they're just going to have to hang. Big setback is anxiety.

Back at it with setbacks! Got another rejection. Funny how those don't sting as much when my survival isn't on the line. I've also been thinking of too many projects I want to do, tech and otherwise, so it's been hard to focus on just one or two. #Onward
So much this. I forget sometimes how much I've done.
I survived several major depressive episodes while broke and unemployed. Depression is a always a low level hum in my heas, but everyday I get up and go is honestly a win.

Yeah, if anyone in my family was having difficulty pronouncing words or rambling like that, I would be really concerned for the actual physical state of their brain. He's deteriorating, and it scares me.

This. The fear of not being the best right off the bat prevents me from even trying something that looks like it might be fun. And sometimes I don't continue activities I do like because I'm not good at them (esp. if in public). I feel a weird secret shame for not being the best.
